flows.period: BofA 'Flow Show' / EPFR week ending Wednesday 22 July 2026 — still the freshest CLEANLY verifiable weekly this run and CARRIED FORWARD (not restamped as current). These flows PRE-date both the 28-31 Jul FOMC selloff-and-rebound round-trip AND the 3 Aug Iran de-escalation/oil crash, so they capture a risk-on EM/China tilt whose durability through the subsequent turmoil is unconfirmed. Weekly flows lag ~2-6 days.
flows.narrative: CARRIED FORWARD (wk to 22 Jul, pre-de-escalation): the freshest verifiable weekly read showed a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record (+$29.6bn EM, +$21.3bn China) on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn. Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn), gold (+$2.0bn, largest since April) and crypto (+$0.9bn) — a barbell chasing EM/China upside while hedging Fed and geopolitical risk. Tech drew +$4.0bn (a record ~$52.8bn over four weeks). BofA's Bull&Bear Indicator sits at an extreme 9.6 (sell-signal active) and July FMS cash is just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian trigger) — stretched-bullish positioning that amplified the FOMC round-trip and Monday's risk-on rip to records. The next Flow Show (and the post-de-escalation read) will show whether the EM/China tilt survived the oil crash and the record-chasing rally; the mid-August FMS is the positioning tell.

regions.note: US-domestic equity funds bled -$7.2bn (wk to 22 Jul) even as the aggregate global-equity number stayed positive — money left the US for EM/China. Pre-dates the 28-31 Jul round-trip; with FMS cash at just 3.6% (contrarian sell), stretched-bullish positioning amplified both the hawkish-hold drop and the rebound to records. US retail firepower has faded — Vanda flagged the biggest single-day single-stock retail SELL since Mar 2020 in late July (semis ~88% of it).

The 2nd-largest weekly EM-equity inflow on record, China-fuelled — the marquee flow and a bid under the HK-tech core into the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal. A pre-shock reading; the delayed wk-to-29/30-Jul Flow Show is the tell on whether it held. (Ignore a garbled '$1tn EM inflow' figure that appeared in one aggregator.)

China's record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever, on stronger-than-expected Politburo stimulus wording — but southbound Stock Connect turned to OUTFLOWS on the chip rout later in the week (and a soft China manufacturing PMI ~49.2 keeps stimulus hopes alive but delivery incremental), a caution that the next Flow Show may show fading.

Continued Japan-equity inflows — the persistent DM haven within the rotation (foreigners on track for a record >¥10tn H1 net buy), on governance reform and BoJ normalization. (Korea separately drew a record multi-week haul.)
Europe joined the US on the outflow side as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex.

A large money-market OUTFLOW — cash redeployed into equities, bonds and gold rather than hoarded. BofA's FMS cash level (3.6% of AUM) still trips the contrarian Cash-Rule sell signal; parked cash yields ~3.5-3.75% — the book's productive dry powder through the round-trip.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued (IG funds on a long weekly inflow streak, govt/Treasury 4 straight) as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge that pre-dates the post-FOMC yield jump (10Y now ~4.75%, a one-year high); HY OAS ~281bp signals no credit stress yet.

The largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April, on the FOMC-hike/geopolitical hedge bid — validated by spot holding ~$4,054 near a record through the round-trip despite Friday's USD-driven ~1.5% dip. Gold's YTD inflow remains a record; BofA flags elevated net-longs. (Crypto funds +$0.9bn the same week.)
